Fixed and interchangeable chokes

A fixed choke is machined into the barrel at the factory, and only a gunsmith can change it. Many older and classic guns are made this way. Such an over-and-under usually has two different constrictions, for example 1/4 and 1/2, and the shooter works with what they have.

Interchangeable chokes (multichoke) are short threaded tubes screwed into the muzzle with a choke key. Most modern competition guns have them. The gun comes with a set of several chokes, and the shooter fits the ones that suit the targets.

Tubes either sit flush (level with the end of the barrel) or are extended: they stick out beyond the muzzle, often by 1–5 cm. Many extended chokes can be turned by hand, and their marking can be read without taking them out.

Safety: Threads and sizes differ between makers and even between models of the same maker. A choke from another system may not fit, or may screw in wrongly, which is dangerous. Buy only chokes made for your gun.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

You may change a choke, the whole gun or a barrel between stands, or between the singles and the doubles, if it causes no delay. Once you have stepped onto the stand, no more changes.

Compak® Sporting

Within a round you may not change the gun, the barrels or the chokes. They are changed only between rounds; the exception is a gun breakdown. So choose chokes that can handle all the targets of the round.

Key points

  • A fixed choke is machined into the barrel; an interchangeable one is screwed in with a key.
  • Chokes from different systems are not interchangeable.
  • Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™: change chokes between stands, not on the stand.
  • Compak® Sporting: no choke changes within a round.

Did you know?

Some Sporting™ shooters do not change chokes during a competition at all and rely on one pair, for example 1/4 and 1/2. That way they think less about equipment and more about the targets.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. When may you change a choke in Sporting™?

    1. Between stands, if it causes no delay
    2. On the stand, just before the double
    3. Only before the first stand of the day
    4. Only with the jury's written consent
    Answer

    Between stands, if it causes no delay

    You may change between stands or between singles and doubles, but not once you are on the stand.

    Chapter 7 · Borrowing or replacing a gun, choke or barrel

  2. May you change chokes within a Compak® Sporting round?

    1. Yes, when moving between stations
    2. Yes, if the next targets are far
    3. No, only between rounds
    4. Yes, at any moment of the round
    Answer

    No, only between rounds

    In Compak® Sporting changing the gun, barrels or chokes within a round is prohibited; the exception is a breakdown.

    Chapter 18 · No changing gun, chokes or barrels during a round

  3. Why should you not fit a choke from another system?

    1. It spoils the look of the gun
    2. The thread may not match, which is dangerous
    3. The referee cannot check its marking
    4. It changes the gauge of the barrel
    Answer

    The thread may not match, which is dangerous

    Choke systems differ; a wrong choke can damage the barrel.
